title: How to access multiple Gmail accounts with Claude
summary: Connect multiple Gmail accounts to any AI coding agent like Claude, Codex, OpenCode or Cursor.
body_markdown:
This tutorial shows how to connect multiple Gmail accounts to Claude, ChatGPT, or any coding agent that supports MCP. The setup is free and should take about 5-10 minutes, after which you’ll be able to query and take actions in multiple email accounts at once.


We’ll use Nango and its Management MCP in this tutorial. The free Nango account supports up to 10 Gmail accounts.


## Step 1: Add Gmail in Nango


Create a[free Nango account](https://app.nango.dev/signup) and log in. Then open **Integrations → Set up new integration** . Search for Gmail and select the entry with the **OAuth 2** label. Both accounts will use this integration.


Keep **Nango-managed OAuth app** selected and click **Create** . Nango’s[pre-approved app](https://nango.dev/docs/guides/auth/auth-guide#nango-managed-oauth-apps) saves you from having to create your own OAuth app in Google Cloud.


## Step 2: Connect both Google accounts


To authorize the first account, open **Connections → Add test connection** and choose the Gmail integration you created.


1. Click **Authorize** , then **Connect** in the **Link Gmail Account** window.
2. Choose your first Google account.
3. Review Google’s permission request and complete authorization.
4. Finish the connection flow and return to Nango’s **Connections** page.


Repeat **Add test connection → Gmail → Authorize** for the second account. In Google’s account chooser, select the other email address. If it is missing, click **Use another account** and sign in. Check the address on the consent screen before continuing.


To connect a Gmail account you can’t sign in to yourself, choose **Share connect link** and send the link to the account owner to complete authorization.[The link expires after 30 minutes](https://nango.dev/docs/guides/auth/share-connect-link) .


If your organization’s policy blocks authorization, ask your Google Workspace administrator to[review the app’s access](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/control-which-third-party-and-internal-apps-access-google-workspace-data) .


Check that Nango lists two Gmail connections, then connect Claude to Nango. Step 4 verifies that the connections belong to different mailboxes.


## Step 3: Enable Nango in Claude


1. In Claude, open **Customize → Connectors** and find Nango, or open the[Nango connector listing](https://claude.ai/customize/connectors/id/mcp-nango-dev) directly.
2. Select **Connect to Claude** and sign in to the Nango account containing your Gmail connections.
3. Review and approve the connection.


Start a new chat. Open **+ → Connectors** in the message box and enable Nango.


On Claude Team or Enterprise, an[Owner or Primary Owner must enable Nango](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11176164-use-connectors-to-extend-claude-s-capabilities) for the organization first.


For Codex, Cursor, or Claude Code, follow[Nango’s Management MCP setup instructions](https://nango.dev/docs/getting-started/coding-agent-setup) . Use the same Nango account and **dev** environment, with permission to access your Gmail connections.


## Step 4: Search both Gmail accounts and draft a reply


The Nango MCP provides prebuilt tools for[Gmail](https://nango.dev/docs/api-integrations/google-mail#others) to search, read, and draft emails using Claude.


Return to your Claude chat and identify each mailbox before searching email:


> List email addresses for all connected Gmail accounts in Nango


Approve read requests if asked, then check that Claude returns the two addresses you connected.


### Search and summarize emails across multiple accounts


The following prompt searches for our fictional tutorial emails. Replace “Nango Gmail demo: November” with a subject you want to find in your inboxes:


> Find the emails with “Nango Gmail demo: November” in the subject in both inboxes. Summarize which ones need a reply, grouped by email address.


Claude identified one demo email needing a reply in each account: a meeting-confirmation request in the first and an article-outline request in the second.


### Have Claude draft a reply in Gmail


Choose a message from the summary and specify its account when requesting a reply. For the article-outline example:


> Draft a reply to “Nango Gmail demo: November article outline” from oyiboemmanuel2394@gmail.com saying “I’ll send the updated article outline tomorrow.” Keep it in the same conversation. Don’t send it.


Open **Drafts** in the intended Gmail account and verify the sender, recipient, and text before sending. Check that the reply appears in the original conversation. If Claude times out or gives an unclear result, check Gmail before retrying to avoid duplicate drafts.


## Reuse your connections across agents and apps


Connect your Gmail accounts to Nango once, then add the Nango Management MCP to Codex, Cursor, or any agent that supports MCP. You can also authorize Google Calendar, Slack, or other apps from[Nango’s catalog of 1,000+ APIs](https://nango.dev/api-integrations) and access them through the same connector.
